findings.title: The shipped CLI host defaults sibling execution to a new OpenCode session
findings.explanation: The built-in host selects opencode as its default command and launches `opencode run` for every sibling invocation. The orchestrator API is abstract, but this is the only concrete host implementation shipped in the package, so callers following the obvious path create child OpenCode sessions.
findings.impact: Execution is coupled to OpenCode process/session semantics, adds latency and nested-agent behavior, and contradicts a direct skill-runtime interpretation of the orchestrator.
findings.remediationSketch: Remove the CLI host from the default execution path. Make the public runtime require an explicit SkillExecutor registry, and retain any subprocess adapter only as an opt-in compatibility adapter with a non-OpenCode name and no default command.

challenges.rationale: The process launch is directly visible in cli-host.mjs and is reached through host.invokeSiblingSkill; the core orchestrator does not itself launch the process.

findings.statusNote: Independent host-path tracing confirmed the finding; the distinction between abstract core and shipped default adapter is material.

findings.title: The orchestrator has no executable registry for most declared sibling skills
findings.explanation: The manifest describes skill metadata and the public module exports orchestration functions, but no runtime handler map exists for declared sibling skills. The host contract therefore delegates execution to an external implementation, and the repository cannot autonomously run the declared route graph by itself.
findings.impact: A caller can receive a policy-compliant orchestration engine that blocks without a host or launches another agent, but cannot obtain the intended end-to-end orchestration from this repository alone.
findings.remediationSketch: Add a versioned executable registry separate from capability metadata. Each supported skill must expose a typed handler with input validation, cancellation, artifact ownership, and typed child-result normalization; unsupported instruction-only skills must be rejected explicitly rather than routed to an implicit LLM session.

challenges.rationale: Inspection found direct callable pipelines only for a subset such as csm-ddd and csm-scan; no general sibling dispatcher or handler registry is present.

findings.statusNote: The manifest is correctly metadata-only, but the missing execution plane prevents the stated autonomous outcome.

findings.title: Final review is not supplied by the built-in CLI host
findings.explanation: The built-in CLI host implements invokeSiblingSkill but not invokeReview. A caller using it without an injected finalReview callback reaches the explicit review-required path after sibling execution.
findings.impact: The advertised autonomous loop is incomplete even when child execution succeeds; the caller must provide a second hidden runtime boundary or stop before terminal verification.
findings.remediationSketch: Make final review another explicit typed registry capability with an independent reviewer identity, or make the intended review executor part of the same in-process runtime while preserving independent provenance checks.

challenges.rationale: The CLI host object has only invokeSiblingSkill, while index.mjs requires finalReview or host.invokeReview for the final-review boundary.

findings.statusNote: The behavior is fail-closed, but it is still an incomplete default execution path.

findings.title: The implementation documents a host contract but does not prove production execution semantics
quotedSnippets: this repository does not provide live host dispatch
findings.explanation: The documentation explicitly says live host dispatch is absent, and tests use synthetic injected host objects. The suite therefore verifies orchestration policy around a boundary, not that the intended sibling skills can execute through a supported runtime.
findings.impact: Green tests can mask the central product gap: the control plane is validated, while the execution plane remains caller-supplied and untested as an integrated capability.
findings.remediationSketch: Add an in-process integration fixture backed by a real executable registry and test complete route execution, cancellation, artifact lineage, review independence, and durable restart without OpenCode or another agent CLI.
findings.statusNote: E3 because the gap is directly documented and statically evidenced, but no production caller was evaluated.

unresolved: The external OpenCode CLI implementation was not modified or executed; findings concern repository architecture at the pinned commit.

rules: No credentials, personal data, or absolute paths
